status.label: Covered by the physical-versus-logical key limitation
status.detail: The report asks to disable End without affecting the numpad 1 key that can produce the same logical End event. Open issue #16432 tracks remapping a specific physical key instead of all keys with the same function.

judgment.rationale: The reported expectation is to disable the physical numpad End function while retaining the other behavior of the same keypad key. Open issue #16432 already tracks distinguishing physical keys from logical key functions; its maintainer explains that the engine currently maps by virtual key and cannot distinguish those inputs. The commenter explicitly links #28040 to that limitation. This is covered by the existing upstream issue rather than a separate Keyboard Manager defect.
evidence: The report says disabling End also prevents the numpad 1 key from working, and removing that remap restores it.
A comment links open issue #16432, which tracks physical-key-specific remapping and documents the virtual-key limitation.
The report has no current-build test.
judgment.recommended_action: Track the physical-versus-logical key distinction under open issue #16432; do not create a competing fix for this duplicate symptom.

fix_assessment.rationale: This issue is covered by the open physical-key distinction issue #16432; the current behavior is a known logical-key limitation, not evidence of a separate regression.

issue_context.summary: Disabling the logical End function reportedly also affects the numpad key that can produce End; this is covered by open issue #16432.
known_information: Disabling End reportedly makes the numpad 1 key stop working; removing the End remap restores it.
Open issue #16432 tracks remapping one physical key without changing all keys with the same logical function.
A comment explicitly links #28040 to the same limitation.
inferences: The numpad key may be emitting End based on Num Lock state, but the report does not include a current-build test.
issue_context.analysis: The linked open issue already tracks the requested physical-key distinction and the maintainer has documented the virtual-key limitation. Keep this issue connected to that shared work rather than proposing a competing fix.
initial_investigation: Read the complete report and both comments.
Inspected open issue #16432; its scope covers changing one physical key without changing other keys with the same function.
Confirmed #16432 is open and the issue comment explicitly identifies the same limitation.
